clue.text: In hospital with curtain round after a bad fall

indicators.note: the curtain-and-hospital piece comes after the word a in the answer
the curtain is wrapped round the hospital letter, enclosing it

parts.note: a valance is a short curtain or drape, as round a bed or pelmet
H is the map and sign abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: A patient in a curtained hospital bed after a nasty tumble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In hospital' paints a ward, but H simply sits inside VALANCE; A comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: An avalanche is a disastrous slide of snow down a mountainside, a fall in the most dangerous sense.

clue.text: Warning notice: face cover finally mandatory

parts.note: an ad is a notice, an advertisement
a visor shields the face, as on a helmet

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of the word mandatory

parts.note: its last letter is Y

explanation.surface: A pandemic-era sign telling people that masks are compulsory.
explanation.definitionFit: An advisory is an official warning or notice, such as a weather or travel advisory.

clue.text: Goes to the gallows, not the first time, in dread

indicators.note: says the opening letter of that verb is dropped

parts.note: someone who goes to the gallows hangs

explanation.surface: A condemned prisoner, reprieved before, facing execution again in terror.
explanation.definitionFit: Angst is a feeling of deep anxiety or existential fear, close kin to dread.

clue.text: The body of male college members useless with scrambled egg

definitions.text: The body of male college members useless with scrambled egg

parts.words: The body of male college members useless with scrambled egg
parts.note: all the men of King's College, Cambridge, read as the nursery-rhyme band who could not put the broken egg Humpty Dumpty together again

explanation.walkthrough: In the rhyme Humpty Dumpty, an egg, falls off a wall and all the king's horses and men cannot mend him; King's is a Cambridge college, once all-male.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names the royal retinue in the nursery rhyme who failed to repair the shattered egg.

clue.text: Circular band nearly full of golden petals

indicators.note: the shortened band holds the golden piece inside it
nearly means the last letter of that band is cut off

parts.note: a collar is a circular band, as round the neck
or is the heraldic term for gold

explanation.surface: A ring of gold surrounding a flower's petals, as in a piece of jewellery.
explanation.walkthrough: OR is heraldry's word for gold, a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: In botany the corolla is the whorl formed by all the petals of a flower together.

clue.text: Resolve to be complicated now?

parts.note: something complicated now is no longer plain: it was plain formerly, and EX means former

explanation.surface: A question about whether to sort out a matter that has become tangled.
explanation.walkthrough: EX means former, so EX-PLAIN describes something that was plain once and is complicated now.
explanation.definitionFit: To explain a puzzle is to resolve it, clearing up what was confusing.

clue.text: Turn computers into a dishonest business

indicators.note: turn tells us to read the computers word backwards

parts.note: Macs are Apple computers

explanation.surface: Someone converting a stock of computers into a crooked enterprise.
explanation.definitionFit: A scam is a fraudulent scheme or swindle, a crooked enterprise run to cheat people.

clue.text: Boy in church worried his rector

indicators.note: worried in the sense of shaken or tugged about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A choirboy who has upset his vicar.
explanation.definitionFit: A chorister is a member of a church choir, traditionally a boy singing treble.

clue.text: Prime minister's surreptitious bug

parts.note: Theresa May was UK Prime Minister 2016-19
fly is British slang for sly or cunning, done on the quiet

explanation.surface: A covert listening device belonging to the Prime Minister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bug' suggests a spy device; here it is an insect.
explanation.definitionFit: A mayfly is a short-lived winged insect, and bug is loosely used for any insect.

clue.text: Pop wants gradually to remove Thatcher at the beginning, that prickly character

indicators.note: places the Thatcher piece at the front of the answer

parts.note: Mrs T was the nickname of Margaret Thatcher, UK Prime Minister
Iggy Pop is the American rock singer
to winkle out is to extract something bit by bit, like a winkle from its shell

explanation.surface: A father eager to oust Mrs Thatcher bit by bit from the start.
explanation.walkthrough: Mrs Tiggy-Winkle is Beatrix Potter's hedgehog washerwoman; 'Pop' reads as father but is the singer Iggy Pop.
explanation.definitionFit: Beatrix Potter's washerwoman is a hedgehog, so a spiny figure in children's fiction.

clue.text: Poet mislaying his third watch

indicators.note: his third refers to the poet's own third letter, which goes missing

parts.note: Virgil was the Roman poet of the Aeneid

explanation.surface: A poet who has lost his third wristwatch.
explanation.definitionFit: A vigil is a period of staying awake to keep watch, as at a sickbed.

clue.text: Type of company stock

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a theatre company performing a rotating set of plays
second meaning: a store or collection of works, a range kept ready

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as finance, company shares; both senses are theatrical or general.
explanation.definitionFit: Repertory names both a resident theatre troupe and the store of pieces it can perform.

clue.text: Let cash fall out of bag

indicators.note: the letters fall out and land in a new order

explanation.surface: Allowing money to spill from a bag.
explanation.definitionFit: A satchel is a bag with a shoulder strap, often carried by schoolchildren.

clue.text: Anyone at first, latest in long sequence sick in crowded tenement

indicators.note: at first picks the opening letter of the word Anyone

parts.note: its first letter is A
nth means the latest in a long series, as in for the nth time
ill means sick

explanation.surface: Anyone, the latest of many, falling sick in an overcrowded building.
explanation.definitionFit: An anthill teems with ants packed together, a natural high-density dwelling.

clue.text: Left TV programme, missing the forecast of good weather

parts.note: red describes the political left

indicators.note: missing says the word the is dropped from the programme title

parts.note: The Sky at Night is the long-running BBC astronomy programme

explanation.surface: Someone walked out of a TV show and missed the weather forecast.
explanation.walkthrough: From the rhyme 'Red sky at night, shepherd's delight', a weather proverb promising a fine day.
explanation.definitionFit: The saying holds that a red evening sky predicts fine weather the following day.

clue.text: To extend my range as Duke, I write poetry

parts.note: to versify is to write verse

explanation.surface: A poetic Duke explaining that he writes verse to broaden himself.
explanation.definitionFit: To diversify is to branch out into new areas, broadening one's scope.

clue.text: Falstaff, say, with bulge not even ready for surgery

parts.note: Falstaff is an opera by Verdi; say marks it as an example

indicators.note: not even keeps only the odd-numbered letters of the word bulge

parts.note: its 1st, 3rd and 5th letters are B, L, E

explanation.surface: Fat Falstaff with a lumpy belly being prepared for an operation.
explanation.walkthrough: Falstaff is Shakespeare's fat knight, but here it is Verdi's opera.
explanation.definitionFit: An operable condition can be treated by surgery, so the patient is fit for the knife.

clue.text: Following plant surveys, ordered this one?

definitions.text: Following plant surveys, ordered this one?

indicators.note: ordered means the letters are put into a new arrangement

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references

explanation.surface: A botanist, after surveying plants, orders a specimen.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: the plant you might order after browsing.
explanation.definitionFit: The Venus flytrap is a carnivorous plant whose hinged leaves snap shut on insects.

clue.text: Unscrupulous type locked in cells, hysterical

indicators.note: the answer is held within the run of letters, as a prisoner in cells

explanation.surface: A crook locked up and hysterical in a prison cell.
explanation.definitionFit: A shyster is a dishonest person, especially a disreputable lawyer or businessman.

clue.text: Old cabs provided reversed over a wide area

indicators.note: in a down entry, over puts that piece above the area piece
reversed says the provided word is read backwards

parts.note: if means provided, as in provided that
acres means a large expanse of land

explanation.surface: Old taxis that, it seems, reversed across a large area.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiacre was a small four-wheeled horse-drawn hackney carriage, a Paris cab of old.

clue.text: Taps closed, gas turned up for warming drink

indicators.note: in a down entry, turned up means the pieces read from bottom to top

parts.note: H and C mark the hot and cold taps
to as in a door pushed to, i.e. shut
CS is the tear gas used in riot control

explanation.surface: Shut the taps, turn up the gas heater, and pour a whisky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gas turned up' looks like heating; CS is tear gas, and the reversal covers all three pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Scotch is whisky distilled in Scotland, a spirit that warms you as it goes down.

clue.text: Agreed to return after short dip

indicators.note: the agreement piece comes after the short piece

parts.note: curt means short, brusque

indicators.note: to return means the agreement word goes back to front

parts.note: yes is the word of agreement

explanation.surface: Someone agreed to come back after a quick swim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short dip' suggests a swim; the dip is a bob before royalty.
explanation.definitionFit: A curtsey is a respectful bob made by bending the knees, a little dip.

clue.text: One in flight of birds finally falling to rook

indicators.note: the final letter drops away

parts.note: avian means relating to birds
R is the chess notation for rook

explanation.surface: One bird in a flock dropping down at last to be caught by a rook.
explanation.definitionFit: An aviator is a pilot, someone who flies aircraft.

clue.text: Apocryphal story very much shortened

indicators.note: shortened cuts the final letter off the phrase

parts.note: to bits means very much, as in I love you to bits

explanation.surface: A tall tale that has been heavily abridged.
explanation.definitionFit: The Book of Tobit is a story in the Apocrypha, the books outside the Hebrew Bible canon.

clue.text: Examiner buttons lip for a term

indicators.note: buttons in the sense of fastening in, so the examiner holds the lip inside

parts.note: a tester examines things
a rim is a lip or edge

explanation.surface: An examiner keeping quiet for a whole term.
explanation.walkthrough: 'buttons lip' reads as keeping silent; here buttons means encloses.
explanation.definitionFit: A trimester is a three-month period, used as an academic term in some systems.

clue.text: Skewer doll on back of truck for return

indicators.note: for return says the whole assembly is read backwards

parts.note: babe and doll are both slang for an attractive woman

indicators.note: back of picks the last letter of the word truck

parts.note: its last letter is K

explanation.surface: Instructions to skewer a doll onto a lorry's tailgate for the return trip.
explanation.definitionFit: A kebab is meat cooked on a skewer, and the word can mean the skewer itself.

clue.text: Superior-sounding greeting

indicators.note: sounding means the superior word is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: higher means superior, above

explanation.surface: A greeting that sounds condescending.
explanation.definitionFit: Hiya is an informal hello, a friendly salutation.

clue.text: Sees great possibility in Roman exploits

indicators.note: a possibility is one possible arrangement, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone spotting great potential in Roman deeds.
explanation.walkthrough: Res gestae is Latin for things done, best known from Augustus's account of his own achievements.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means deeds or achievements, the recorded acts of a Roman.
